newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Oppn rejects budget-rates link.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Oppn rejects budget-rates link.

text.p: Australian Labor Opposition Leader Kim Beazley said on Monday there was no connection between the Liberal-National government's planned fiscal tightening and lower interest rates.

"There is clearly no essential immediate connection between the two and (Prime Minister) John Howard was trying to create that all over the weekend," Beazley said, citing the former Labor government's experience in the late 1980s.
"So John Howard's talk about interest rates, about jobs is just claptrap designed to avoid real issues which he must confront," Beazley told reporters.
Howard said on Saturday that Labor's plans to vote against budget measures in the Senate, the upper house of parliament, imperils lower interest rates and the jobs they could produce.
Beazley said the government's budget papers, announced on August 20, showed that proposed industrial relations changes would constrain activity, and not create jobs.

"What this budget paper says is this: If everything goes through in this budget, if all John Howard's industrial relations changes go through, what will happen as a result of that is that the economy will contract, we'll have growth rate for the next four years less than Labor achieved in the last
"How is that going to create more jobs?"
"He is basically putting out this matra of his on jobs and on interest rates to conceal the fact that he is seriously running into trouble with the nasties in the budget," Beazley said.

Beazley said on Friday the Labor Opposition was proposing to oppose about a quarter of the government's total fiscal consolidation programme: measures worth A$7.3 billion over four years, compared with the full programme's four-year value of A$23.4 billion.
The government aims to produce a budget surplus of about A$1 billion in the fiscal year to June 30, 1999, compared with the 1995/96 deficit of A$10.3 billion.
